name: The Elder Wand
owner: Passed by conquest, most recently to Harry Potter
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
description: Elder wood with a thestral tail-hair core. The most powerful wand ever made, and the one with the shortest list of owners who died of old age.
lore: Its allegiance transfers to whoever defeats the previous master — a rule that has quietly rewritten centuries of wizarding history, usually in a back alley.

name: The Resurrection Stone
owner: The House of Gaunt, then Albus Dumbledore
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
description: A small black stone that calls back an echo of the dead. It does not return them; it only makes their absence louder.
lore: It spent years set into a ring as a Horcrux, which is roughly like using a priceless heirloom as a doorstop.

name: The Cloak of Invisibility
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: Unlike ordinary demiguise-hair cloaks, this one never fades, never frays, and hides its wearer from anything — including, reportedly, Death.
lore: The only Hallow that was used as intended: to protect, and to sneak out after curfew.

name: The Marauder's Map
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
description: A living map of Hogwarts that shows every corridor, every secret passage, and every person walking them — by name, in real time.
lore: It is also enchanted to insult anyone who tries to read it without the password, which is arguably its best feature.

name: Time-Turner
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
description: An hourglass on a chain. One turn, one hour backwards. Lent to students only when the alternative is a timetable that requires being in two places at once.
lore: The Ministry's entire stock was destroyed in a single fall down a staircase, which says something about magical contingency planning.

name: The Sorting Hat
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: Godric Gryffindor's own hat, given enough of the founders' intelligence to read a first-year's mind and argue with them about the result.
lore: It takes your preference into account. That is not a loophole — it is the whole point.

name: The Pensieve
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
description: A shallow stone basin that holds siphoned memories, so their owner can walk back into them and look at what they missed the first time.
lore: Memories in a Pensieve are objective in a way memories in a head never are — you see the room, not just your corner of it.

name: The Mirror of Erised
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: Shows the deepest, most desperate desire of whoever stands before it — and nothing else, least of all the truth.
lore: Men have wasted away in front of it. The happiest person alive would use it as an ordinary mirror.

name: The Philosopher's Stone
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: Turns any metal into gold and produces the Elixir of Life. Its maker used it to live six centuries and, by all accounts, to enjoy them.
lore: Flamel agreed to its destruction with the calm of a man who had already had quite a long day.

name: The Goblet of Fire
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
description: A rough-hewn wooden cup filled with blue-white flame. It selects the champions, and its choice is a binding magical contract.
lore: It has no opinion about whether you meant to enter. Ask Harry.

name: The Sword of Gryffindor
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
description: Goblin-made silver set with rubies. It takes in only what makes it stronger — which is why basilisk venom turned it into a Horcrux-killer.
lore: It presents itself out of the Sorting Hat to a true Gryffindor in need, and refuses to be summoned by anyone else.

name: Tom Riddle's Diary
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
description: A blank diary that writes back. The first Horcrux, and the only one designed to be handed to a stranger.
lore: Destroyed by a basilisk fang in the Chamber of Secrets, which is the sort of sentence that only makes sense at Hogwarts.

name: Slytherin's Locket
owner: Salazar Slytherin, then the House of Gaunt
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
description: A heavy gold locket marked with a serpentine S. Worn as a Horcrux, it soured the mood of anyone who carried it for long.
lore: Regulus Black swapped it for a fake and left a note. It took years for anyone to read it.

name: Hufflepuff's Cup
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
description: A small golden cup with two fine handles and a badger engraved on the side. Kept in the Lestrange vault under a multiplying curse.
lore: Helga used it for potions. Its later owner used it for something considerably worse.

name: Ravenclaw's Diadem
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
description: A lost circlet said to sharpen the mind of whoever wore it. Hidden for centuries in the Room of Requirement, under a mountain of other people's secrets.
lore: The Grey Lady stole it from her mother and hid it in an Albanian forest. It has been badly looked after ever since.

name: Marvolo Gaunt's Ring
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
description: A gold ring set with a cracked black stone — a Horcrux and, unknown to its maker, the Resurrection Stone itself.
lore: Putting it on cost Dumbledore a hand and, eventually, a year.

name: Nimbus 2000
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: The racing broom that made a first-year the youngest Seeker in a century. Sleek handle, ash twigs, excellent acceleration.
lore: Retired abruptly by a Whomping Willow, which has never apologised.

name: Firebolt
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
description: Nought to a hundred and fifty miles an hour in ten seconds, with a braking charm that actually works. The international standard for professional Quidditch.
lore: Arrived anonymously at Christmas and was immediately confiscated for testing. It was, in the end, just a very good broom.

name: The Deluminator
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: A silver device that takes light out of any source and holds it, returning it on a second click. Useful for street lamps and for hiding.
lore: Dumbledore left it in his will to a man who would one day need a light to find his way back to his friends.

name: The Vanishing Cabinet
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
description: One of a matched pair. Step into one and step out of the other — provided both are intact, which for years they were not.
lore: Repairing the broken twin took a sixth-year most of a school year, and let an army into the castle in an evening.

name: Remembrall
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: A glass ball of smoke that turns scarlet when you have forgotten something. It is scrupulously unhelpful about what.
lore: Arguably the most frustrating object ever sold by owl order.

name: Howler
owner: Anyone with a grievance and an owl
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
description: A red envelope that shouts its message at full volume in the sender's voice, then tears itself to shreds. Ignoring one makes it worse.
lore: Best opened somewhere private. The Great Hall at breakfast is not somewhere private.

name: Omnioculars
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
description: Brass binoculars that replay, slow down and annotate what you just watched. Essential when the Snitch moves faster than your eyes.
lore: Ten Galleons at the World Cup, and worth every one if you missed the Wronski Feint.

name: Floo Powder
owner: Regulated by the Floo Network Authority
firstAppearance: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
description: A pinch thrown into a fire turns the flames emerald and opens the grate to any connected hearth. Say the destination clearly.
lore: Mispronounce it and you end up in Knockturn Alley. Ask Harry about that, too.
